oracles.tool: go mod edit -json, go work edit -json, go list -e -m -json all

notes: oracle: the go command itself, tier A (calibration/oracles/go-mod, go1.26.3): `go mod edit -json` and `go work edit -json`, its own parse of each file, for the definitions and the module-to-requirement references; `go list -e -m -json all`, its own evaluation of the module graph (module mode with GOWORK=off and -mod=mod, and workspace mode where a go.work reaches the module), for what a declaration resolves to: 159 require, 194 replace and 39 use edges to a directory of the subject that holds a go.mod. The parse is golang.org/x/mod/modfile, the package the dialect reads with, so it attests what the dialect models (every directive and block form) and not the parser; positions, which the tool does not print, come from an independent line scan (no modfile) aligned entry for entry with the tool's list, 0 scan mismatches.

subjects are sparse checkouts of every go.mod, go.sum, go.work and go.work.sum (kubernetes/kubernetes v1.37.1: 45 files read, 39 go.mod and 6 go.work, 7.6 MB on disk; cli/cli v2.99.0: 2 go.mod, 0.5 MB). L3 rests on kubernetes alone (cli/cli is one application module with no replace and no workspace): 392 edges the tool resolved, all found, 2 more drawn.

xref_precision .9949 (392 of 394): the two edges the dialect draws and the tool does not are hack/tools/golangci-lint/go.mod's require of the published k8s.io/apimachinery, which the dialect resolves by module path to staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/go.mod (its own go.work `use .` keeps the go command from climbing to the repository's workspace, so the tool resolves it in the registry: a require means a module by path alone, the doc engine's module-source rule), and hack/tools/instrumentation/go.mod's `replace k8s.io/kubernetes => ../../..`, which nothing requires, so the tool lists no replacement and the dialect records the local pointer.

the tool cannot resolve 3 modules of the build lists (hack/tools/instrumentation's k8s.io/client-go and k8s.io/streaming at v0.0.0, code-generator/examples' k8s.io/streaming: no replace redirects them); `go list -e` reports them with an error and evaluates the rest, so those go.mod and go.work files are attested for what they do resolve.

not modelled, with reasons in dialects/go-mod/PROVENANCE.md: the // indirect flag (a ModuleDep keeps the incumbent's name, version signature and tier), exclude, retract, toolchain, godebug, tool and ignore directives, go.sum, vendor/modules.txt; a require whose module path two go.mod files of the repository declare resolves to nothing (the doc engine's unique-root rule; cli/cli's .github/codeql test module declares the root's own path).
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
